bull_bear.body: Focus on reducing debt and improving return on capital employed
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Dependence on cyclical auto industry, moderate capital structure, client concentration risk, exposure to raw material price volatility
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company's natural hedge from exports partly offsets the impact of raw material price volatility
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The Board has recommended an interim dividend of Rs 4 per share.
- Deleveraging is the stated financial priority within the quarter commentary: interest cost down Rs 2 cr sequentially with further reduction expected in upcoming quarters.
- Chairman frames capital discipline as a "strong financial foundation and prudent financial management" supporting growth "while maintaining focus on profitability and long-term value creation".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Established engineering capabilities and a skilled workforce, positioning it favorably as a cost-competitive sourcing alternative amid global supply-chain diversification.
- Deep customer relationships and a dominant revenue share from the resilient commercial vehicle segment, which recorded its highest-ever sales volume in India during FY26.
- A strategic transition to 100% green energy, which is expected to deliver significant power cost optimization and improve profitability margins.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical instability and conflict in West Asia — Escalation involving Iran and Israel, and threats to the Strait of Hormuz, cause volatility in crude oil prices, logistics costs, and global supply chains, directly impacting input costs and export demand.
- Global trade policy uncertainty and tariff pressures — Protectionist trade policies and tariff-related disruptions among major economies weaken export market conditions, particularly in Europe and North America, and reduce business share in key regions.
- Volatility in commodity and energy prices — Fluctuations in steel, crude oil, and energy costs create short-term margin pressures and increase operating costs, given India's dependence on imported crude oil.
- Subdued export demand in key markets — Weak Class 8 truck market in North America, declining business share in Europe, and overall geopolitical tensions continue to weigh on export volumes and revenue diversification.
- Foreign exchange rate volatility — Higher exchange rates and currency fluctuations impact export competitiveness and the value of foreign exchange earnings, affecting profitability.
- Climate-related disruptions and environmental compliance — Climate-related events pose operational risks, while the ongoing pursuit of ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certifications reflects the need to manage environmental and safety compliance costs.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: MM Forgings Ltd (MMFL) is a manufacturer of steel forgings, supplying safety-critical, high-strength components primarily for the automotive sector. The company's core business is producing forged parts for commercial vehicles, passenger vehicles, and off-highway/agricultural equipment, leveraging its engineering expertise to serve both domestic original equipment manufacturers and international customers. It operates with a strong focus on operational efficiency and is transitioning to 100% green energy for its manufacturing operations.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Commercial Vehicle:** Forged components for MHCV and LCV trucks
- **Passenger Vehicle:** Forged components for passenger cars and utility vehicles
- **Agri and Off-Highway:** Forged components for tractors, construction, and mining equipment
- **Others:** Forged components for railways, defence, and energy sectors
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- D V S Industries Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary; factory in Pantnagar, Uttarakhand; precision equipment, in-house tool room inspection. Amalgamation with MM Forgings filed with NCLT, awaiting order.
- Suvarchas Vidyut Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary; manufacturing of electrical and electronic components and subassemblies for industrial, consumer and automotive applications.
- Abhinava Rizel Private Limited — subsidiary: 88% stake; design and manufacturing of parts/components for EV electric power train, electric motors, controllers/drives, gearbox for automotive, industrial, marine, aerospace. Sampling/testing of motors for two/three-wheelers; production anticipated in FY 2026-27.

- A strategic transition to 100% green energy, which is expected to deliver significant power cost optimization and improve profitability margins.

outlook.body: Outlook: Stable; Strategy: Focus on expanding forging and machining capabilities, improving operating margins, and reducing customer concentration risk
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: Increasing demand for heavier forgings in machined condition, expansion into new markets, and potential for growth in the electric vehicles segment
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strategic transition towards 100% green energy, entering long-term arrangements with captive power generating units to consume green power and optimize power consumption across manufacturing facilities.
- Expanding product portfolio by leveraging established forging capabilities and engineering expertise, strengthening presence in core product segments while pursuing opportunities in emerging mobility solutions.
- Enhancing market reach through new product development, increased localization initiatives, and deeper engagement with domestic and international customers.
- The Company has a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy, hosted on its website, and dividends are declared in compliance with that policy.
- The Company is currently in the process of obtaining certification for ISO 14001 (Environmental Management System) and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety Management System), reaffirming its commitment towards environmental sustainability, workplace safety and continual improvement in operational standards.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company has embarked on a strategic transition towards 100% green energy during FY26, entering into a long-term arrangement with captive power generating units and starting consumption of green power from Q4FY26 onwards. This initiative is expected to deliver significant optimization in power consumption and improve operational efficiency across manufacturing facilities, with visible improvements in operating performance from the upcoming FY onwards. The Company continues to focus on expanding its product portfolio by leveraging its established forging capabilities and engineering expertise, strengthening its presence in core product segments while pursuing opportunities in emerging mobility solutions. It also continues to enhance market reach through new product development, increased localization initiatives, and deeper engagement with domestic and international customers. The Company is currently in the process of obtaining certification for ISO 14001 (Environmental Management System) and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety Management System). Additionally, the Board has approved an enabling resolution for raising funds up to an aggregate amount of ₹600 crores through Qualified Institutional Placement or other permissible modes, subject to necessary approvals and market conditions, to meet future business requirements. The Scheme of Amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary DVS Industries Private Limited with the Company is pending NCLT approval, with an appointed date of 01 April 2024, which upon effectiveness will combine the authorized share capital of DVS with that of the Company, increasing the Company's authorized share capital by ₹2,50,00,000.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sustained demand from commercial vehicle, passenger vehicle, and industrial sectors presents significant opportunities for long-term growth.
- Transition to renewable energy is projected to enhance profitability margins, with visible improvements in operating performance from the upcoming FY onwards.
- Company's focus on operational efficiency, value-added products, and improved product mix supported overall business performance and profitability during FY26.
- Growth in automotive production, infrastructure development, defence manufacturing, railways, renewable energy projects, industrial capital expenditure, and export opportunities expected to support sustained demand for forged components.
- Global supply-chain diversification trends creating new opportunities for Indian forging manufacturers as international customers seek reliable and cost-competitive sourcing alternatives.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

open.item: H1 EBITDA 19% (17.5% operational) vs 21%; EBITDA/ton INR 38,000 vs 40,500; margins expected to only improve from these levels if sales have bottomed.
Domestic addressable market shrinking as multi-axle vehicles give way to tractor-trailers (fewer front axles); domestic CV static, ~+/-2%.
US 50% tariff borne by customers (CIF contracts); expected absorbed until ~March, then resourcing/renegotiation likely; margins could pressure if sustained.
Net debt to come down ~INR 50-75 Crores via inventory compression; scope for at least INR 50 Cr inventory reduction.
Converting rupee loans to forex to cut interest; H1 interest INR 39 Cr; targeting FY26 interest within INR 70 Cr, run-rate INR 50-60 Cr (saves ~INR 12 Cr/yr).
H2 FY26 revenue expected ~INR 750-800 Crores, taking full-year close to previous year's level (give or take a few percent).
Plan to add wind/solar green power (from ~3 cr to up to 10 cr units) to insulate against 5%/yr TN power hikes; ~150 bps EBITDA benefit, likely from next year.
US Class VIII truck market seen as bottom (Q2 worst); customer restocking from November, reasonable levels by June 2026.
Abhinava Rizel acquired first customer (~INR 20-30 Cr annual potential); sample parts to be delivered end-Nov 2025, then production; also commercializing controllers.
Sales expected to grow by at least INR 300 Crores in next 12-18 months; decline reversing to growth from FY27 onwards.
FY27 to add 15,000-20,000 tons capacity via 16,500t press plus a ~4,000t forging line, pushing capacity to ~140,000 tons; targeting 80,000-90,000 tons output.
FY26 capex ~INR 170 Cr (INR 100 Cr H1, ~INR 70 Cr H2); FY27 capex ~INR 100-120 Cr; ~INR 70 Cr investment remaining at fag end of expansion cycle.
Order book of ~INR 300 Crores revenue, of which ~INR 200 Crores expected to realize in FY27.
Net debt ~INR 850-855 Crores declared as peak debt; no more borrowing intended, hold at these levels; no significant reduction next 2 years (store cash / cut working capital instead).
New export customer acquisitions expected to add at least INR 100 Crores of export sales in FY27 and FY28.
Abhinava Rizel/EV powertrain (incl controllers) long-term revenue of Rs.1,000-2,000 Crores over 7-10 year horizon.
Scheme of Amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary DVS Industries Private Limited with the Company, pending NCLT approval, with appointed date 01 April 2024.

Management expects to end FY2023 close to 72,000 tonnes production, with Q4 similar to prior quarters.
FY2024 production/sales targeted at 85,000-90,000 tonnes (sales +/-5%), from ~76,000 tonnes production last year.
EBITDA per tonne guided flattish at ~Rs.35,000 for full year; 19% EBITDA margin reasonably on track (needs push to 36-37k/tonne).
H1 EBITDA 19% (17.5% operational) vs 21%; EBITDA/ton INR 38,000 vs 40,500; margins expected to only improve from these levels if sales have bottomed.

- Suvarchas Vidyut Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary; manufacturing of electrical and electronic components and subassemblies for industrial, consumer and automotive applications.
- Abhinava Rizel Private Limited — subsidiary: 88% stake; design and manufacturing of parts/components for EV electric power train, electric motors, controllers/drives, gearbox for automotive, industrial, marine, aerospace. Sampling/testing of motors for two/three-wheelers; production anticipated in FY 2026-27.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained demand from commercial vehicle, passenger vehicle, and industrial sectors presents significant opportunities for long-term growth.
- Transition to renewable energy is projected to enhance profitability margins, with visible improvements in operating performance from the upcoming FY onwards.
- Company's focus on operational efficiency, value-added products, and improved product mix supported overall business performance and profitability during FY26.
- Growth in automotive production, infrastructure development, defence manufacturing, railways, renewable energy projects, industrial capital expenditure, and export opportunities expected to support sustained demand for forged components.
- Global supply-chain diversification trends creating new opportunities for Indian forging manufacturers as international customers seek reliable and cost-competitive sourcing alternatives.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has embarked on a strategic transition towards 100% green energy during FY26, entering into a long-term arrangement with captive power generating units and starting consumption of green power from Q4FY26 onwards. This initiative is expected to deliver significant optimization in power consumption and improve operational efficiency across manufacturing facilities, with visible improvements in operating performance from the upcoming FY onwards. The Company continues to focus on expanding its product portfolio by leveraging its established forging capabilities and engineering expertise, strengthening its presence in core product segments while pursuing opportunities in emerging mobility solutions. It also continues to enhance market reach through new product development, increased localization initiatives, and deeper engagement with domestic and international customers. The Company is currently in the process of obtaining certification for ISO 14001 (Environmental Management System) and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety Management System). Additionally, the Board has approved an enabling resolution for raising funds up to an aggregate amount of ₹600 crores through Qualified Institutional Placement or other permissible modes, subject to necessary approvals and market conditions, to meet future business requirements. The Scheme of Amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary DVS Industries Private Limited with the Company is pending NCLT approval, with an appointed date of 01 April 2024, which upon effectiveness will combine the authorized share capital of DVS with that of the Company, increasing the Company's authorized share capital by ₹2,50,00,000.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established engineering capabilities and a skilled workforce, positioning it favorably as a cost-competitive sourcing alternative amid global supply-chain diversification.
- Deep customer relationships and a dominant revenue share from the resilient commercial vehicle segment, which recorded its highest-ever sales volume in India during FY26.
- A strategic transition to 100% green energy, which is expected to deliver significant power cost optimization and improve profitability margins.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
